title: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file exists to open. Europe PMC says the paper is not open access and has no PMC copy, no supplementary flag, no database cross-references and no text-mined accessions beyond antibody/cell-line RRIDs (lab-reagent identifiers). NCBI elink from PubMed ID 42617596 returned zero links to BioProject, SRA (Sequence Read Archive) and GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus); the PubMed XML record has an empty DataBank list. Zenodo returned only two unrelated 2007/2018 DNIC chemistry records, Dryad zero, Figshare search endpoint 404. The one supplementary file surfaced by web search (mmc1.pdf on cell.com) returns HTTP 403, and the cell.com full-text page returns 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the science comes from the abstract alone: electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR, a spectroscopy method that detects unpaired electrons) detection of dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) in conventional versus germ-free mice, feces/E. coli DNIC generation from nitrate plus iron citrate, Western-diet mouse supplementation experiments, HepG2 cell and human hepatocyte spheroid steatosis assays, and the mechanistic chain through soluble guanylyl cyclase, leucine uptake and mTORC1. No methods text, no figure source data and no sample sizes were retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. Nothing downloadable: paywalled Cell article (403 on full text and on the only supplementary PDF), no PMC copy, no accession in any repository (checked BioProject, SRA, GEO via NCBI elink; Zenodo, Dryad, Figshare by search). There is no dataset to inspect, let alone model.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and almost certainly fail. The measurements are EPR (electron paramagnetic resonance) spectra and per-animal physiology readouts shown as figure panels; any label would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots or by tabulating numbers that are not published as a table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable. No feature table, no sequences, no SMILES (chemical structure strings) and no per-sample metadata are available.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable. Units (e.g. nanomoles of DNIC per gram of tissue) are presumably stated in figure axes, but no numeric file exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on scale as well. A mechanistic mouse study of this design has tens of animals per arm, i.e. order 10^1-10^2 observations in total, far under the ~1,500-row bar. No count was verified because no file exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small if it existed; size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable. No download and no API record to compare against the paper's claims.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle: DNIC levels come from direct EPR spectroscopy and the cardiometabolic outcomes from physical assays, not from another model's output. This is the one Part A item the paper would pass, but it is moot given A1.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: there is no accessible data, so no model could be trained or evaluated.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a gut bacterium's genome to predict whether it converts dietary nitrate and iron into a heart-protective iron-nitric-oxide complex.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: bacterial genomes or metagenome-assembled genomes (their gene content, especially nitrate-reductase genes) for strains and stool communities tested in the paper's assay. Number of examples: unknown, and no table of strains or genomes is published.
plain_idea.predict: Intended output: how much dinitrosyl iron complex (an iron atom carrying two nitric oxide groups) a strain or community makes from nitrate plus iron citrate, as measured by electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy on the incubation.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Microbiome and cardiometabolic groups could screen strains in silico for ones that make this protective molecule, instead of running spectroscopy on each. But the paper publishes no strain-by-yield table, so this project cannot start from it.

ml_idea: The only sensible idea would be to predict per-strain dinitrosyl iron complex (DNIC) output from bacterial genome content, with the nitrate-reductase-deficient mutant as a built-in negative control, then score public gut metagenomes for DNIC-generating capacity. It fails immediately: the paper is paywalled, the supplement is blocked, and no strain-level or sample-level measurements were deposited anywhere, so there is no label column and only tens of observations even in principle.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data was obtainable, so there is nothing to size. All probes were metadata lookups costing seconds.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether any machine-readable file exists at all: one NCBI elink call plus a Zenodo/Dryad DOI search. Both came back empty in under a minute, which killed the candidate.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright. This is a paywalled mechanistic mouse and cell-culture study with no open full text, no deposited accession in GEO, SRA or BioProject, no Zenodo/Dryad/Figshare record, and a supplementary PDF that returns HTTP 403. Even if the supplement were obtained it is figure panels from experiments with tens of animals, so A5 (enough rows) and A2 (label already a column) would fail too: the quantity of interest, tissue dinitrosyl iron complex level by electron paramagnetic resonance, would have to be digitised out of plots. Good biology, no dataset.
